candidate.title: Nuc-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned poster row headed Nuc-Seq: single-nucleus RNA library preparation from the depicted preserved tissue through an enrichment-ready indexed DNA fragment. Inventory: a single-cell/poly(A) RNA pictogram describes the RNA target at left; the material route is Tissue → Fixation and freeze → Lyse and centrifuge → Nuclei → Sort nuclei → representative poly(A) mRNA → cDNA synthesis with an LNA-marked GGG/CCC junction → PCR → Tagmentation → Gap repair and PCR → fragment labeled P5, Index 2, Index 1, P7. This row has one route and no depicted split, pool, or alternative branch. DR-Seq (partly cropped at top), inDrop, and Div-Seq are separate neighboring catalogue rows, with no arrows connecting them to Nuc-Seq; they are image context, not additional target methods. The literal poster citation points to Habib N et al. (2016) bioRxiv; the recovered Nuc-Seq preprint and the published sNuc-Seq component of the Div-Seq paper establish the intended RNA method. The candidate Illumina collection page has the matching RNA heading and matching schematic, but its Krishnaswami citation identifies a related fresh/frozen nuclear-RNA implementation; its complete preparation is not merged into the fixed/frozen poster route. Smart-Seq2 and Nextera-style library preparation remain components, not extra method targets. The graph ends at the depicted library, not an invented sequencing or analysis operation.

method_scopes.rationale: All seven local operations belong to the assigned Nuc-Seq row at schematic scope. Habib preprint terminology Nuc-Seq and published terminology sNuc-Seq identify the single-nucleus RNA component underlying Div-Seq; this does not add the adjacent EdU/Click-iT Div-Seq workflow as a target. The Habib full text supports frozen/fixed tissue, nuclei isolation, FACS and modified Smart-Seq2. The matching collection description supports the LNA/Smart-Seq2/Tn5 component interpretation but cites a different fresh/frozen nuclear-RNA protocol. That protocol provides a supported correspondence for downstream chemistry; none of the fixed-history local operation instances is asserted to be its complete implementation. The drawing is not a universal sequence for all methods called Nuc-Seq, particularly the unrelated DNA method of the same name.
